name: ICW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Held by Magus at the fed's one surviving complete pay-per-view, defended successfully against Royal Rumble winner Todd Newkirk. "Bad Boy" Mark Bagwell is billed as the belt's first-ever champion and Curt Crane recounts winning it at the fed's own "ICW Blood Bowl" tournament in 1996; no document in the held record narrates how the title passed from Crane to Magus.

name: ICW North American Championship
epitaph: Created at the fed's own Season Beating's PPV (17 January 1997) to replace a vacated ICW International Championship: the broadcast announces the International belt vacated ahead of the match and its winner crowned with a new North American belt. Peter Bell, the reigning International/North American champion introduced pre-match, retained by disqualification over Brian Anthony.

name: ICW Light-Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Named on the fed's own Season Beating's line-up as the Light-Heavyweight Championship but called the "Cruiserweight" title twice in the same broadcast's own commentary -- an in-house naming inconsistency, recorded rather than resolved. Held by "ShotGun" Chris Scott going into a defence against Curt Crane whose result does not survive in the recovered text.

name: ICW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Crowned for the first time in this collection's own holdings at Season Beating's, the finals of a tournament: Boxoffice Bound over Damage Incorporated, decided by Zulu Nation's interference.
